title: Contribution of sleep-related biomarkers to the pathophysiology of ME/CFS: Linking neuronal function to vascular pathology
summary:
The aim of the project is to understand the biological mechanisms associated with brain function in ME/CFS (Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome). It investigates symptoms like cognitive issues, fatigue, headaches, sleep disorders, and sensory hypersensitivity. Of particular interest are the activities of specific brain networks during sleep, as they can provide insights into brain function. For example, sleep spindles reflect the integrity of networks involved in memory, sleep stability, and sensory processing.
The project uses various methods, including brain imaging with MRI, blood flow measurements, assessments of brain energy metabolism, as well as biochemical and genetic analyses in order to characterize underlying pathomechanisms in ME/CFS. Another goal is to create individual risk profiles to enable personalized therapies in the future. A total of 75 patients with ME/CFS and 75 control subjects will be studied, with a follow-up after one year. By integrating these data, we aim to better understand the relationship between neurophysiological and neurobiological features of ME/CFS and to capture the interindividual heterogeneity of the condition.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- ME/CFS according to the Canadian criteria for ME/CFS
Exclusion criteria:
- Non-removable electrical implants
- Metal implants made of non-MRI-compatible material that cannot be removed
• Permanent make-up
• Claustrophobia
• Pregnancy
• Tattoos within 30 cm of the head
• Presence of a neuropsychiatric disorder (in patients: except ME/CFS)
• Presence of a neurodegenerative disease / dementia
• Presence of any other serious illness (in patients: except ME/CFS)
• Acute suicidality
• Current intake of benzodiazepines, benzodiazepine receptor agonists, or antipsychotics
• Drug abuse
